Sulabhā
------------------------------------------
Even in the ancient days, women had the freedom to take to monastic life. This is illustrated by the story of सुलभा as narrated by भीष्म to युधिष्ठिर (Mahābhārata, Śāntiparva

).
Sulabhā was the daughter of the king प्रधान. She had taken to monastic life and was moving about at will after attaining spiritual illumination. Once she heard that the king Dharmadhvaja जनक of मिथिला was a knower of ब्रह्मन्. She went to him just out of curiosity to test him and entered into his मिन्द् through her मिन्द्. A long conversation ensued between them about spiritual and philosophic topics. This has been described in detail by the Mahābhārata as mentioned above.

Śulbasūtras
------------------------------------------
The वेदाङ्गस् are the subsidiary treatises that help us in understanding the वेदस् more clearly because the latter are couched in archaic and even symbolic language.
The कल्पसूत्रस् form the last part of the वेदाङ्गस्. They are again divided into four streams, the last of which is the शुल्बसूत्रस् (also spelt as Śulvasūtras).
Śulba means the thread used for measurement.
The शुल्बसूत्रस् deal with the construction of yajñavedis (platforms for the performance of वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस्). They reveal an astonishing knowledge of geometrical sciences.
Seven शुल्बसूत्रस् are now available. They are closely related to the Śrauta-sūtras, the first of the four branches of the कल्पसूत्रस्.
They are:
Āpastamba Śulbasūtras
Baudhāyana Śulbasūtras
Kātyāyana Śulbasūtras
Maitrāyaṇa Śulbasūtras
Mānava Śulbasūtras
Vādhūla Śulbasūtras
Varāha Śulbasūtras
See also KALPASŪTRAS.

Śūlagava
------------------------------------------
It is a very ancient sacrifice performed to please रुद्र/Śiva (who was called Śūlin, the wielder of śūla or the spear or the trident) when cattle were stricken with pests or diseases.
It could be performed during the bright half of a month and on an auspicious नक्षत्र.
Though an ox used to be sacrificed in the most ancient period, it was substituted by a goat or even cooked ड़ोओद् in the later days due to the repugnance of the people against it. The deity was called ईशान (same as शिव).
The rite soon went out of vogue.

-1445)
------------------------------------------
Śūlapāṇi is one of the three important writers on the धर्मशास्त्रस् from Bengal (See JĪMŪTAVĀHANA.). He wrote several small treatises on various topics of the धर्मशास्त्रस्. Twelve of his tracts, ending with the word ‘viveka’ are well-known. Some of them are: Dattaka-viveka, Dolāyātrāviveka, Durgotsava-viveka, Ekādaśīviveka, Pratiṣṭhāviveka, Prāyaścittaviveka, Śrāddhaviveka and Śuddhiviveka.
The Śrāddhaviveka is the most famous of these and has been printed. The Prāyaścittaviveka is an extensive work and deals with various kinds of prāyaścittas or expiations for sins.
His Dīpakalikā is a commentary on the Yājñavalkyasmṛti and is regarded as his earliest work.
Śūlapāṇi has been respectfully referred to by रघुनन्दन (A.
-1580) another famous author of धर्म-śāstras from Bengal.
